corrected_value.title: Two attempted retro-priming replications show theory-relevant anomalous connectivity.

decisions.quote:
2) The second experiment in this study (Experiment 2), a conceptual replication of the work reported by Jolij and Bierman (2019), yielded
marginal evidence (p = .064) of anomalous connectivity—of the same
order of magnitude as found in Jolij and Bierman.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this work. In Experiment 2, Grote (2021) conducts an empirical conceptual replication of Jolij and Bierman (2019) ('Two attempted retro-priming replications show theory-relevant anomalous connectivity', Journal of Scientific Exploration, 33(1), 43-60; References, p. 309, lines 678-680), testing whether correlations between questionnaire psychological variables and random-event-generator physical variables show anomalous connectivity and comparing the resulting p = .064 effect directly to Jolij and Bierman's finding (Introduction, p. 290, lines 110-111; Results, pp. 300-301, lines 396-415; Discussion, p. 306, lines 561-563). This study is completely distinct from shipped row 2407 (Walach et al., 2020, 10.1037/cns0000199) and from sibling target 0 (von Lucadou, 2006, 10.1063/1.2388760), which both concern the Experiment 1 button-push micro-PK paradigm.

decisions.location: Methods, Data Analysis Experiment 1; Introduction; Discussion
decisions.quote:
The analysis for this experiment had been specified and tested
during the data acquisition phase. In particular the data had not been
looked at or analyzed in any way before the unblinding, in agreement
with the blind analysis protocol. The analysis of the experiment had
been implemented in software (Matlab) as outlined below. The analysis
code, as well as all the experimental data, have been pre-registered and
are accessible at https://osf.io/xwhn6 for Experiment 1 and at https://
osf.io/cj8kd for Experiment 2.
For Experiment 1, the data-analysis procedure closely follows the
way the data was analyzed for the latest experiments described in von
Lucadou (2006), except for the evaluation of statistical significance of
the matrix of correlation factors (which was performed as outlined
below). The choice of variables resembles the choice of the experiment
reported in Walach et al. (2020), with the exception that one of the
psychological and physical variables each was replaced with new ones,
as indicated below.
From the data recorded during the experiment (see above), the
decisions.reason: The current Introduction positively identifies Walach2020as a new empirical replication of vonLucadou2006button-push correlation-matrix findings, with a changed but explicitly retested significance analysis; current Experiment1follows this same effect and variable structure. Existing2407already represents Walach2020, the closest actual empirical retest. Reusing2006feedback or analysis components and jointly citing2006/2020for the same Experiment1effect does not create a distinct earlier finding. Under the codebook chain rule, explicit ancestry plus one shared tested empirical claim settles representation without requiring that the older source be called background in every sentence. No unique2006finding is identified and tested separately in the current report. The current software/statistic check on2020data does not create a second2006original. This is empirical-chain representation, not alternate-report equivalence, an assumption from publication year, or dismissal of an older positive finding as mere theory. The raw undeterminable opinion remains unchanged.
